title: Same and Different
objectives: I can sort objects into groups and tell how I sorted them.
I can match two things that are alike.
I can say what is the same and what is different.
I can count a group of objects out loud.
rationale: Sort, match, same, different, and count are the working words of early math and science, and children need them before they sort objects in later units. The first three are things children do with their hands, and same and different name what they notice. Count is included because sorting always ends in counting each group. The unit builds on position words (beside, between) and calm, since children work side by side at a table.

passage.title: Sam and the Buttons
paras: Sam has a pile of buttons. He will sort them into two cups. The red ones go in one cup, and the blue ones go in the other.
Sam counts the red buttons and finds four. Then he looks for a match for each blue button.
Two blue buttons are the same, but one is different: it is big.

qs.q: Sam will sort the buttons. How does he sort them?
qs.why: The red buttons go in one cup and the blue buttons go in the other, so he sorts by color.

qs.q: How many red buttons does Sam count?
qs.why: Sam counts the red buttons and finds four.
Two blue buttons are the same, and the different one is big.

teacher.overview: Children learn five working words of math and science by sorting, pairing, and counting real objects, then hear them in a short story about a boy and his buttons. Teaching is hands-on and spoken; no reading or writing is needed.

notes.va.sort.v: Use a bin of mixed buttons or blocks and a few cups. Children often make one group and call it sorting; ask 'What is the other group?' and 'How did you decide?'. Sort has other meanings, such as a kind, which are not taught here.
notes.va.match.v: Use a set of paired objects, such as socks, lids, and jars. Match is to pair alike things; children may match by a different rule, such as one thing that goes with another, so name the rule each time.
notes.va.same.adj: Hold up two identical objects. Same means alike in the way we are talking about, so say 'the same color' or 'the same size'. Avoid asking children to say same for two that are only a little alike.
notes.va.different.adj: Use two objects that differ in one way. Ask 'How are they different?'. Children often say different for anything, so connect it to the same-different pair and say both words.
notes.va.count.v: Move one object at a time and say one number per object. Count has other meanings, such as to matter, which are not taught here. Have children count a group two ways to show the total stays the same.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I have buttons. I will sort them into groups. These buttons are red, so they go here. These are blue, so they go there. Now I count the red group: one, two, three. Three red buttons. Let's sort and count together.'
discuss: Can you sort the same things another way?
Show me two things that are the same and one that is different.
misconceptions: Sort means put everything in a line.
Same means exactly alike in every way, so nothing can be the same.
extend: Play a sorting game with a sock box: sort by color, then by size, and count each group.
Make a class chart: things that are the same, things that are different.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit beside, between, and calm by asking children to place sorted groups beside or between each other while working calmly. Use sort, same, and different again in unit 5 when children sort objects by how they feel to touch.

frames: These two are the same because ___.
wida.oral: Partner A holds up three objects, two alike and one not. Partner B says which two are the same and which one is different, using the frames.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (clasificar, emparejar, igual, diferente, contar) have not been reviewed by a native speaker; clasificar and agrupar may both be used for sort.
Sense boundary: sort, match, and count are taught only in their verb senses of grouping, pairing, and saying numbers; other meanings (a kind of thing, a game match, to matter) are left out.
Sense boundary: same is paired with different as an opposite pair; the phrase 'at the same time' is not taught.
